chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about Al-Hijr: is it part of the House (Kaaba), or is there something (else) from the House in it? He said: No, not even (the size of) a nail clipping. But Ismail (peace be upon him) buried his mother in it, and he disliked that it should be trampled upon, so he built a chamber upon it. And therein are the graves of the Prophets (peace be upon them).

key_terms.الْبَيْت: Al-Bayt (The House, referring to the Kaaba)
key_terms.الْحِجْر: Al-Hijr (the semi-circular wall adjacent to the Kaaba)
key_terms.قُلَامَةُ ظُفُرٍ: Qulamatu dhufurin (the size of a nail clipping)

ai.seo_question: Is Al-Hijr considered part of the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Al-Hijr is distinct from the Kaaba proper, explaining its enclosure by Prophet Ismail (AS) specifically to preserve the grave of his mother Hagar (SA) from being trampled during circumambulation. This narration highlights the historical sanctity of the site, noting it also contains the graves of prophets, thereby distinguishing its original purpose as a protective enclosure rather than an integral structural component of the House of God.
